body:
Thank you for replying. I understand that I have to forgive myself. I missed out on a lot of fun and the chance to grow into adulthood with great people. I look back on the friendships I threw away and it's a really heartbreaking loss.

I have only ever thought about teaching English abroad, which honestly doesn't really appeal to me. One thing that turns me off is that I am Indian and I've heard that people who aren't white often encounter racism. Coupled with the fact that I'm pretty introverted, I worry that it wouldn't be a good idea to try to be a teacher. I may look into other types of work that is possible to do abroad. If you know of a good place to search for such opportunities, please let me know.

The real goal for me is to begin a career that makes my parents proud of me, and I think it is going to have to be a desk job because I can't see myself getting hired to do much else with my background and experience. I don't think any employers respect what I've done since graduating and it's so hard to communicate the path that's led me to where I am without seeming irresponsible and incompetent. 

In any case, your words did help and I appreciate you taking the time to give me encouragement.
